newsitem.title: EGYPT: PLO leader says world must cut ties with Israel.
newsitem.headline: PLO leader says world must cut ties with Israel.

text.p: A PLO leader said all countries must cut all ties with Israel because it had abandoned the Middle East peace process, a step that could lead to another war in the region.

"The Israeli government has turned its back on the peace process and (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu has totally destroyed this process," Farouk Kaddoumi, head of the Palestinian Liberation Organisation's political affairs department, told reporters in Cairo on Sunday.

"We demand that all (Israeli) offices be shut, all international ties suspended, all political activities halted and we demand that particularly from Europe and the United States as sponsors of the peace process," he added.

"The United States appears to be encouraging Israel to go in the direction opposite to peace. This heralds a return to violence and sharpens the levels of tension which could lead to a new war," said Kaddoumi, who came to attend a ministerial meeting of the Cairo-based Arab League.

Arab and Islamic countries in meetings at Islamabad and Rabat said they would reconsider ties with the Jewish state if it did not stop construction work on a Jewish settlement in disputed Arab East Jerusalem.

Ties between the Palestinians and Israelis plunged into crisis after Netanyahu's government broke ground on the settlement at the site called Jebel Abu Ghneim or Har Homa. The building work has also set off 10 days of violence and a suicide bombing which killed three Israelis in Tel Aviv.

United States, Israel's main ally, sent Middle East meditor Dennis Ross to help resume talks but Kaddoumi said he was a "biased Zionist" and that Washington was siding with Israeli intransigence when it vetoed U.N. resolutions demanding Israel stop the housing project.
"Dennis Ross can go to hell, he's a biased Zionist who came to execute a plot ... to harm the peace process," Kaddoumi said.

"The United States is using unequal scales to measure the process for it is the sponsor of the peace process yet at the same time is its contradicting itself and encouraging Israel by the veto and by not pressuring it," he added.

Washington's position on the Jebel Abu Ghneim settlement has angered its Middle Eastern allies and Egyptian newspapers said that the regular Arab League meeting would call for suspending normalisation with Israel.
